item.title: Updated Rubric for Worked Problems and Projects
item.description:
19 Oct 2023

Choosing and Explaining an Appropriate Problem (30%)

30 points total - An appropriate problem is often one one on the border of analytical and numerical methods (or one that can be simplified or extended to be either). If you can solve it completely analytically, then consider how it can be extended for a computing activity. If you have questions or thoughts, please ask Danny, Alia, or Ian.

item.title: Worked Problem Assignment 2
item.description:

We have spent much of our time on a dynamical systems view of ODEs. In this assignment, you will choose an ODE and work through a dynamical analysis of the system.

Remember that a worked problem means the scale of a detailed (e.g., parts a-h) homework problem.

item.title: Project 1 - Classical Mechanics and ODEs
item.description:
Due 29 Sep 23

Project 1 will focus on the the topic of ordinary differential equations in physics. Differential equations are often how we describe nature because nature often changes continuously (quantum mechanics notwithstanding). We focused in class on various oscillators. Your job is to develop a project that investigates some nonlinear differential equation of your choosing. Our expectation is that this ODE is nonlinear, at least 2nd order or two coupled 1st order equations, and that is of interest to you personally or professionally. Below is a list of potential candidates.

item.title: Worked Problem Assignment 4
item.description:
Due 13 Oct 23

The electric potential, $\Phi$, is often a better quantity to work with when solving electrostatics problems. As we have seen, we can do direct integration to find the potential at a given point. We’ve also seen that we can solve for the potential using the Laplace equation. In this worked problem, you will explore the potential in a specific situation of your choosing.

Grading Rubric

Remember that a worked problem means the scale of a detailed (e.g., parts a-h) homework problem.

item.title: Project 2 - PDEs, Laplace's Equation, and the Method of Relaxation
item.description:
Due 27 Oct 23

Updated Rubric

Project 2 will focus on the topic of partial differential equations, specifically Laplace’s equation. For this project, you will be given a choice to work alone or in a pair. If you work in a pair, we expect the work to be more in-depth and to explore more aspects of the problem. For example, you should consider one of the extensions listed below to add to your project. If you work alone, we expect the same level of depth as with project 1.

item.title: Worked Problem Assignment 5
item.description:
Due 3 Nov 23

We have developed an approach to find the normal modes of a linear oscillating systems. For this problem you will choose a system that oscillates with at least 3 oscillators and explore the motion and dynamics of that system. You cannot choose coupled springs; it must be a system that you have not already explored in class.

Updated Rubric

Remember that a worked problem means the scale of a detailed (e.g., parts a-h) homework problem.

item.title: Worked Problem Assignment 6
item.description:
Due 10 Nov 23

We have shown that we can use a Fourier Transform to decompose a function into its frequency components. We’ve graphed the solutions, and we’ve seen how we can construct signals with certain properties. In this assignment, you are asked to use these tools to solve a problem of your choosing. Consider a scenario where a signal of some sort is being generated and you want to understand the frequency content of the signal. You can use the tools we have developed to do this.

item.title: Project 3 - Waves and Fourier Analysis
item.description:
Due 17 Nov 23

Updated Rubric

Project 3 will focus on the topic of waves and Fourier analysis. You will need to do an analysis of some data of your choosing. You may start this work during the class week of 10/13 after we go through some initial work.

What do you need to do?

Think about the ways that an FFT can be used. How we can extract frequency information, clean signals, and more. You can use the FFT to explore any data you want. You can use this project to explore any data you want. It only needs to be 1D data, but you have to provide a full analysis and explanation of what you are doing.

item.title: Project 4 - Probabilistic Modeling
item.description:
Due 14 Dec 23

Updated Rubric

Project 4 emphasizes probabilistic models. We’ve done work with counting statistics (flipping coins and rolling die). We’ve modeled radioactive decay and decay chains. We’ve developed Monte Carlo simulations to do integrals and to model different systems. In this project, you are free to choose a particular probabilistic model and apply it to a new physics situation of your choosing. You may be creative in your choice of model and situation, but you must be able to justify your choices.
